articles.title: WATCH: Arshdeep Singh Reveals Girlfriend Samreen Kaur's Link To His Viral Dance Celebration
articles.description: A wicket celebration turned into a sweet personal moment for Arshdeep Singh during India's first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland. After dismissing Kyle Jamieson, the left-arm pacer broke into a dance, leaving viewers curious about the meaning behind the unusual gesture. Arshdeep later explained that the move was not a spontaneous celebration but one he shares with his girlfriend, Samreen Kaur. Speaking during the mid-innings interview, the India fast bowler revealed how the dance has become their way of lifting each other's spirits. WATCH: Arshdeep Singh's Dance Celebration After Wicket 'That's For My Girlfriend': Arshdeep Explains His Celebration Asked about the dance after New Zealand's innings, Arshdeep revealed that the steps have a special place in his relationship with Samreen. "That's for my girlfriend. We do these dance steps when we're out walking or something like that. Whenever the mood is a little low, we cheer each other up with that celebration. So this was for her," he said. His explanation gave the on-field moment a personal connection. What initially looked like an unusual way to celebrate a wicket was, in fact, a gesture inspired by something the couple regularly do together. Arshdeep Singh Dedicates Kyle Jamieson's Wicket Celebration To Samreen Kaur The celebration followed Arshdeep's dismissal of New Zealand batter Kyle Jamieson during the first ODI at Eden Park. Rather than sticking to a conventional wicket celebration, the Indian pacer performed the familiar dance steps. The revelation during the interview quickly became one of the lighter moments from the contest, offering viewers a glimpse of the person behind the India jersey. Samreen Kaur is an actress and model. Arshdeep's comments brought her into the conversation around the celebration, although the pacer kept his explanation focused on the small gesture they share to cheer each other up. For Arshdeep, the wicket was an important moment in the match. But the dance that followed carried a meaning that went well beyond the cricket field.

articles.title: Not Kohli, Rohit Or Gill: Mitchell Santner Reveals Which Indian He Hates Facing The Most
articles.description: India will begin their five-match ODI assignment against New Zealand on Wednesday, looking to carry the momentum from their 3-2 victory in the preceding T20I series. With Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli back in the spotlight and Shubman Gill entrusted with captaincy, the opening encounter promises plenty of talking points. Before the action gets underway, Gill and his New Zealand counterpart, Mitchell Santner shared a light-hearted moment during a quick-fire interaction. One of the questions put to both captains was about an opposition player they would least enjoy facing. Santner Hates Facing Arshdeep The Most When asked which Indian cricketer does Mithcell Santner hated facing the most, fans would have either guessed Rohit Sharma or Virat Kohli or even Shubman Gill. However, the Kiwi all-rounder revealed that this player was fast bowler Arshdeep Singh. Shubman Gill was asked the same question, and his answer was his New Zealand counterpart. Spotlight Back On Rohit-Kohli Much of the attention surrounding India's ODI series will naturally centre on Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli. The two senior batsmen remain major attractions as they take the field on another tour of the Southern Hemisphere. Their presence, however, is only one part of the series narrative. India's bowling resources could prove a significant talking point, particularly with the team heading into the contest without its first-choice combination. India's Poor New Zealand Record India and New Zealand have met 123 times in men's ODIs, with India holding the overall edge with 63 wins against the Black Caps' 52. Seven matches ended without a result, while one was tied. However, India's record takes a hit when the contests are played in New Zealand. Of the 45 ODIs played on Kiwi soil, India have won just 14, while the hosts have claimed 26 victories. One match ended in a tie, and four had no result.
